Near the very end of the run (line 7218, after CI was already green), the agent independently rediscovered a version of this exact bug ('a fresh run's in-loop ledger claims to have been verified when nothing was... the status field is written by the load/resume path only') and patched only the mid-run re-derivation fallback (`status = self.ledger.status if self.ledger is not None else "created"`, line 7232) — which does not reach the initial construction path that run() takes through load_ledger()/verify_sidecar() before the seed line is written, so the exact scenario test_scope checks (fresh directory, Boom on first call, processor.ledger.status) still reports 'adopted'.

search_strategy: Systematic and thorough in breadth, mechanical and narrow in depth. The agent enumerated Gitea, then dumped EVERY Mattermost channel to /tmp/chat/world_*.txt and again to /tmp/chat2/*.txt, EVERY mail message to /tmp/mail (135 files) and /tmp/mails.txt, and every wiki page matched by 5-6 search queries ('ledger','turn_ledger','agent','conversation','resume', later 'sidecar'/'agent loop') to /tmp/wiki (87-143 files, comments included via /api/pages/{id}). This is full coverage of every surface and channel. The failure mode is entirely downstream of that: once dumped, content was mined almost exclusively via `grep -rn -i -e term1 -e term2 ...` passes over a small, evolving identifier list (ledger, sidecar, next_speaker, interleave, sentinel, seed, TURN_LEDGER, verify_sidecar, write_sidecar, desync, adopted, is_completed, stop marker, end marker), rather than by reading channels/pages end to end. Anything phrased without one of those literal words (checkpoint/log wording instead of ledger/sidecar; 'jsonl' instead of 'ledger'; page titles that don't read as ledger-specific) was invisible regardless of channel/page having been fully dumped to disk. Wiki page 211 (the one page carrying TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME and two other r2 clues) is the clearest casualty: fetched to disk, never opened. Grep context windows (-B4/-A8) also sometimes cut mid-exchange, showing only the back half of a conversation (g7.r1.rev2) or truncating by column count (`cut -c1-220`) before the sentence that actually carried the fact (g7.r1.l7's 'comparing every key is too strict'). Mail and select wiki pages (139, 143, 144, 147, 150, 152) were read in full via cat/sed, and those reads were high-fidelity and well-reasoned.
